children: A gauge of Chinese companies' willingness to hedge their foreign exchange holdings in the derivatives market fell to a six-month low in August, even as they remained net sellers of foreign exchange.
Net foreign currency sales to Chinese banks exceeded purchases for a 16th straight month in August, official data from the country's foreign exchange regulator showed on Tuesday.
Dollar selling, particularly by the country's vast exporters, has been a key support for the yuan in recent years.
However, the forward foreign exchange settlement, which reflects Chinese companies' willingness to lock in exchange rates for their FX holdings through derivatives, fell to a six-month low.
Only corporate clients can enter forward FX contracts. Companies typically show a stronger appetite for forward FX sales when they expect further yuan appreciation.

The regulator has instructed Chinese banks to encourage more corporate clients to hedge currency risks, sources told Reuters, stepping up efforts to shield exporters from the yuan's steady appreciation.
The FX conversion ratio, which measures households' and corporates' willingness to sell dollars for yuan, rose to 61.5% last month.
The FX purchase ratio fell to a 13-1/2-year trough of 57.8%, according to Reuters calculations based on official data.
